extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party submitters, patent owners, and USPTO examiners (reexamination personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements and USPTO handling rules for submissions of prior art and requests for ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents under 35 U.S.C. 301/302 and 37 CFR 1.501/1.510, including who may file, what must be included, timing, service, fees, and handling by Technology Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission content
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.501 submission must be limited to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information, and must include the requisite citation description and information (and proof of service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission lacks these elements it is not proper for entry. Use forms PTO/SB/08A, 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent) to list cited prior art. Include translations of non-English pertinent parts. See MPEP § 2294 and § 2217.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry when submission filed prior to reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed prior to an order in any pending reexamination, it should be immediately entered into the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt entry into the reexamination file is required; no storage delay. This applies to third-party and patent-owner filings that meet the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when submission filed after reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed after the date of an order for reexamination in a pending reexamination proceeding, the submission is not entered into that reexamination but is retained (stored) in the Technology Center until the reexamination is concluded, then placed in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send notification letters to the patent owner and third-party submitter (if known). If a third-party requester exists, send them a copy per 37 CFR 1.550(f). Place an e-tag in the reexamination file history to remind placement after conclusion. Citations filed after the order that are not entitled to entry in reexamination will not be considered by the examiner during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for stored submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a citation is stored because it was filed after a reexamination order, the patent owner and third-party submitter (if known) should be notified of the storage and non-entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a duplicate copy was submitted or service on patent owner was omitted, follow the procedures: send duplicate to patent owner or make stored original available for copying. Notification enables parties to consider other procedural vehicles (e.g., 37 CFR 1.555 or 1.933 or filing a separate reexamination request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner submissions entry rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed by the patent owner, it should be entered in the file regardless of whether it is filed prior to or after an order for reexamination; no notification to the patent owner is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent-owner-filed citations are entered even when filed after a reexamination order (subject to applicable reexamination rules such as use of 1.555/1.933 where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of improper 1.501 submissions (third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 37 CFR 1.501 submission by a third party is not proper (not limited to permitted items, lacks description/information, or lacks proof of service), it will not be entered and handling depends on service and identity of submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitter unknown => discard and notify patent owner. If identity known but service not included => return to submitter with notification; patent owner not notified. If identity not known and no service => discard. If service included and identity known, return original to submitter with notification of non-entry. Follow specific procedures in MPEP § 2206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on patent owner requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any third-party submission of prior art or section 301 written statements placed in the patent file must be served on the patent owner at the correspondence address per 37 CFR 1.33(c); submissions failing to include proper proof of service per 37 CFR 1.248(b) will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address service to the correspondence address in the file (see MPEP § 2222). If service is not shown, the submission may be returned or discarded depending on other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and limits on filing court papers into patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept copies of notices of suits, notices regarding proceedings involving the patent, and copies of litigation decisions for entry into the patent file, but will not enter non-merit decisions, party argument papers, or papers that contain arguments unless those arguments have an entry right in reexamination via the proper rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only decisions/notifications without additional comment. Highlighting or marking text goes beyond bare notice. The Office may return, expunge, or discard submissions deemed too lengthy. Papers from foreign courts may be returned/expunged/discarded at the Office's discretion. If arguments are to be considered in reexamination, they must be submitted via the correct procedural vehicle (e.g., rules provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics and policy goals of ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination procedures provide for: reexamination of patents; essentially ex parte proceedings; minimized processing costs/complexities; maximized respect for the reexamined patent; and prompt, timely determinations under 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the listed basic characteristics (anyone can request; prior art limited to patents/printed publications; substantial new question required; ex parte proceedings if ordered; decision on request within 3 months; scope of claim cannot be enlarged; public access to files with electronic availability through PAIR). Parties must avoid litigation tactics and unauthorized submissions not provided for by regulations (see 37 CFR 11.18(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an ex parte reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a request for ex parte reexamination during the period of enforceability of the patent, unless prohibited by estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'any person' includes corporations and governmental entities. The only prohibited filers are those barred by the estoppel provisions once estoppel attaches. The requester’s name will not be maintained in confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts of a reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability; (2) identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested plus a detailed explanation of pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to each claim; (3) copies of every relied-upon patent/printed publication (with English translations of necessary parts); (4) a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims) and any disclaimers/certificates; (5) a certification that the request was served in its entirety on the patent owner (name/address indicated) or duplicate supplied; and (6) a certification that estoppel provisions do not prohibit filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element must be satisfied for the request to be complete; otherwise the requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. Failure to comply results in no filing date and the request may instead be treated as a 1.501 citation if compliant with that rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must 'point out each substantial new question of patentability' based on prior patents and printed publications and explain how the cited documents raise that substantial new question for each proposed ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should clearly identify what the requester considers a substantial new question and provide explanation for each identified substantial new question; a requester must not argue that references do not raise a substantial new question (i.e., do not argue against issuance of an order). See MPEP § 2216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed explanation of pertinency to each claim
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim identified, the request must provide a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to that claim, and if relying on patent owner statements submitted under § 1.501(a)(2), must explain how those statements are used to determine claim meaning and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriate, the requester may also point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art. The explanation must be sufficiently specific for each claim and proposed ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy and formatting requirements for submitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a copy of every cited patent or printed publication (with translations of necessary parts), and a copy of the entire patent including front face, drawings, and specification/claims in double-column format; all copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-English documents require English translations of necessary parts. Include any disclaimers, certificates of correction, or reexamination certificates. Failure to provide proper copies/format may render the request incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment and filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be accompanied by the reexamination fee set in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1); the filing date of the request is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements of 37 CFR 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request lacks the fee or required elements, the requester will be notified and usually given time to complete; failure to comply results in no filing date and possible treatment as a 1.501 citation. If the patent owner files and includes a proposed amendment under 1.530, excess claims fees under 1.20(c)(3)&(4) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: No abandonment or withdrawal after fee-paid request
rubrics_metrics.description: After the request and entire fee for requesting reexamination are received, no abandonment, withdrawal, or striking of the request is possible regardless of who requested it, except in limited circumstances (e.g., final court decision rendering claims finally invalid prior to order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In limited cases (e.g., final court decisions) a reexamination order may be vacated or the proceeding terminated per MPEP § 2286.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative and power of attorney requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an attorney or agent files a request identifying another party, the attorney/agent must have a power of attorney from that party or act in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34; registration number, name and signature must be provided for representative capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing of the request will not be delayed due to absence of a power of attorney, but providing it is desirable. A patent owner may not be represented by someone not registered to practice before the Office because those individuals cannot sign amendments or other papers in a reexamination proceeding on the patent owner’s behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel certification by third-party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party requester must certify that estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is required under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(6). Estoppel may arise from prior inter partes review or post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of inquiries from third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not discuss or answer inquiries from third parties about specific reexamination proceedings; refer such inquiries to Technology Center Quality, Central Reexamination Unit (CRU), or Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only strictly procedural questions (not directed to any specific proceeding) may be handled by CRU SPRS or TC QAS. Employees who conducted a concluded reexamination should not discuss whether a certain reference was considered or whether a claim would have been allowed over that reference. Improper inquiries by practitioners are prohibited (see 37 CFR 11.804).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on submissions and litigation tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not countenance litigation tactics in reexamination proceedings; submissions not provided for by the regulations or appearing excluded should be accompanied by a petition to accept/waive the regulation or should not be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple submissions like replies and sur-replies not provided for in regulations are not permitted. Parties are expected to adhere to 37 CFR 11.18(b) and applicable reexamination rules; improper argument-type submissions will be returned/expunged/discarded or must be submitted via proper procedural vehicles.
